messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Stimulus, and Action Cable (`async` adapter in single-process Puma). All CSS, JS, QR SVGs (`rqrcode`), and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- All `fetch()` and WebSocket URLs resolve against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so URL-embedded Basic Auth works reliably across HTTP and WebSockets.
- `question_active_controller.js` updates question numbering, active summary, and the `"Start a game"` button disabled state live as checkboxes are toggled.
- Player finished place text (`"Place 2 of 5"`) is kept in a single inline `.result-card__label` element (with the large decorative place numeral `aria-hidden="true"` above it) so visible `innerText` and exact-text browser selectors match `"Place 2 of 5"` without embedded newlines.

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`, `action_cable.worker_pool_size = 8`). `config/database.yml` allocates `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` SQLite connections to serve Puma threads and Action Cable workers cleanly without contention.

- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.

require "securerandom"
require "set"

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :winners_count,
    presence: true,
    numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, allow_blank: true }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Quiz has no active questions" if active.empty?

    attempts = 0
    begin
      attempts += 1
      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(
          code: generate_code,
          status: "lobby",
          winners_count: quiz.winners_count
        )

        active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question: question,
            position: q_index + 1,
            body: question.body
          )

          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(

              position: o_index + 1,
              body: option.body,
              correct: option.correct?

          end
        end

        game
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      raise if attempts >= 5
      retry
    end
  end

    Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join

  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"

  def finished?
    status == "finished"

  def validate_and_normalize(data)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)

  def validate_title(data)
    unless data.key?("title")

    end

    title = data["title"]
    unless title.is_a?(String)
      errors.add(:base, "Title must be a string")

    end

  def validate_questions(data)
    unless data.key?("questions") && data["questions"].is_a?(Array)

    end
  end

class ModeratorChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(id: params[:game_id])
    unless @game && authorized_moderator?(@game.id)
      reject
      return
    end

    stream_from @game.moderator_stream_name
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def authorized_moderator?(game_id)
    return true if connection.moderator_authenticated

    token = params[:token].to_s
    return false if token.empty?

    verified_game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).verified(token)
    verified_game_id.present? && verified_game_id.to_i == game_id
  end
end

class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    @subscription_key = "#{connection.connection_id}:#{object_id}"
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      unless @game.finished?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      stream_from @game.visitors_stream_name
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    @game.reload
    return if @game.finished?

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end

class ModeratorChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(id: params[:game_id])
    unless @game && authorized_moderator?(@game.id)
      reject
      return
    end

    stream_from @game.moderator_stream_name
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def authorized_moderator?(game_id)
    return true if connection.moderator_authenticated

    token = params[:token].to_s
    return false if token.empty?

    verified_game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).verified(token)
    verified_game_id.present? && verified_game_id.to_i == game_id
  end
end

class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    @subscription_key = "#{connection.connection_id}:#{object_id}"
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      unless @game.finished?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      stream_from @game.visitors_stream_name
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    @game.reload
    return if @game.finished?

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end

class GamePresence
  DEFAULT_WS_STALE_SECONDS = 10.0
  DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL_SECONDS = 10.0
  DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2.0

  class << self
    attr_writer :ws_stale_seconds, :http_ttl_seconds, :sweep_interval_seconds

    def ws_stale_seconds
      @ws_stale_seconds || DEFAULT_WS_STALE_SECONDS
    end

    def http_ttl_seconds
      @http_ttl_seconds || DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL_SECONDS
    end

    def sweep_interval_seconds
      @sweep_interval_seconds || DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS
    end

    def connect_ws(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        entry[:ws][connection_id] = { player_id: player_id, connected_at: now, last_seen_at: now }
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def heartbeat_ws(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        if entry[:ws][connection_id]
          entry[:ws][connection_id][:last_seen_at] = now
        else
          entry[:ws][connection_id] = { player_id: player_id, connected_at: now, last_seen_at: now }
        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def disconnect_ws(game_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        removed = entry[:ws].delete(connection_id)
        if removed
          player_id = removed[:player_id]
          connected_at = removed[:connected_at]
          still_has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
          if !still_has_ws && entry[:http][player_id] && entry[:http][player_id] <= connected_at
            entry[:http].delete(player_id)
          end
        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def touch_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        entry[:http][player_id] = now
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def leave_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
        entry[:http].delete(player_id) unless has_ws
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return 0 unless entry

        count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      end
    end

    def sweep!
      now = monotonic_now
      changed_game_ids = mutex.synchronize do
        changed = []
        games.keys.each do |game_id|
          entry = games[game_id]
          before_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          entry[:ws].delete_if { |_cid, meta| (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) > ws_stale_seconds }
          entry[:http].delete_if { |_pid, ts| (now - ts) > http_ttl_seconds }
          after_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
          changed << game_id if before_ids.size != after_ids.size
        end
        changed
      end

      return changed_game_ids if changed_game_ids.empty?

      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        Game.where(id: changed_game_ids).find_each do |game|
          game.broadcast_moderator_state! if game.lobby? || game.question_open?
        end
      end

      changed_game_ids
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GamePresence] sweep error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      []
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        games.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def games
      @games ||= {}
    end

    def game_entry(game_id)
      games[game_id] ||= { ws: {}, http: {} }
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end

    def count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value do |meta|
        ids[meta[:player_id]] = true if (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds
      end
      entry[:http].each do |player_id, ts|
        ids[player_id] = true if (now - ts) <= http_ttl_seconds
      end
      ids.size
    end

    def active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value { |meta| ids[meta[:player_id]] = true }
      entry[:http].each_key { |pid| ids[pid] = true }
      ids
    end

    def ensure_sweeper_started
      return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

      sweeper_mutex.synchronize do
        return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

        @sweeper_thread = Thread.new do
          Thread.current.name = "game-presence-sweeper"
          loop do
            sleep sweep_interval_seconds
            sweep!
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def sweeper_mutex
      @sweeper_mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end
  end
end

        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
        entry[:http].delete(player_id) unless has_ws
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return 0 unless entry

        count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      end
    end

    def sweep!
      now = monotonic_now
      changed_game_ids = mutex.synchronize do
        changed = []
        games.keys.each do |game_id|
          entry = games[game_id]
          before_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          entry[:ws].delete_if { |_cid, meta| (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) > ws_stale_seconds }
          entry[:http].delete_if { |_pid, ts| (now - ts) > http_ttl_seconds }
          after_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
          changed << game_id if before_ids.size != after_ids.size
        end
        changed
      end

      return changed_game_ids if changed_game_ids.empty?

      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        Game.where(id: changed_game_ids).find_each do |game|
          game.broadcast_moderator_state! if game.lobby? || game.question_open?
        end
      end

      changed_game_ids
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GamePresence] sweep error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      []
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        games.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def games
      @games ||= {}
    end

    def game_entry(game_id)
      games[game_id] ||= { ws: {}, http: {} }
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end

    def count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value do |meta|
        ids[meta[:player_id]] = true if (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds
      end
      entry[:http].each do |player_id, ts|
        ids[player_id] = true if (now - ts) <= http_ttl_seconds
      end
      ids.size
    end

    def active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value { |meta| ids[meta[:player_id]] = true }
      entry[:http].each_key { |pid| ids[pid] = true }
      ids
    end

    def ensure_sweeper_started
      return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

      sweeper_mutex.synchronize do
        return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

        @sweeper_thread = Thread.new do
          Thread.current.name = "game-presence-sweeper"
          loop do
            sleep sweep_interval_seconds
            sweep!
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def sweeper_mutex
      @sweeper_mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Quiz::ExporterTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "exports exact keys, values, and order" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")

    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: 'Which HTTP status code means "Too Many Requests"?', active: true)
    assert q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "418", correct: false },
      { body: "429", correct: true }
    ])

    q2 = quiz.questions.build(body: "What does CSS stand for?", active: false)
    assert q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Cascading Style Sheets", correct: true },
      { body: "Computer Style System", correct: false },
      { body: "Creative Style Syntax", correct: false }
    ])

    # Reorder so q2 comes before q1
    assert q2.move_up!

    json = Quiz::Exporter.new(quiz).to_json
    parsed = JSON.parse(json)

    assert_equal %w[questions title], parsed.keys.sort
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", parsed["title"]
    assert_equal 2, parsed["questions"].size

    first_q = parsed["questions"][0]
    assert_equal %w[active options text], first_q.keys.sort
    assert_equal "What does CSS stand for?", first_q["text"]
    assert_same false, first_q["active"]
    assert_equal [
      { "text" => "Cascading Style Sheets", "correct" => true },
      { "text" => "Computer Style System", "correct" => false },
      { "text" => "Creative Style Syntax", "correct" => false }
    ], first_q["options"]
    first_q["options"].each do |opt|
      assert_equal %w[correct text], opt.keys.sort
      assert_includes [ true, false ], opt["correct"]
    end

    second_q = parsed["questions"][1]
    assert_equal %w[active options text], second_q.keys.sort
    assert_equal 'Which HTTP status code means "Too Many Requests"?', second_q["text"]
    assert_same true, second_q["active"]
    assert_equal [
      { "text" => "418", "correct" => false },
      { "text" => "429", "correct" => true }
    ], second_q["options"]
  end

  test "exports empty quiz with empty questions array" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Empty Quiz")
    parsed = JSON.parse(Quiz::Exporter.new(quiz).to_json)

    assert_equal({ "title" => "Empty Quiz", "questions" => [] }, parsed)
  end

  test "preserves option position order even when opposite of id order" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Option Order Quiz")
    question = quiz.questions.create!(body: "Pick one", position: 1, active: true)
    question.options.create!(body: "Second by pos", correct: false, position: 2)
    question.options.create!(body: "First by pos", correct: true, position: 1)

    parsed = JSON.parse(Quiz::Exporter.new(quiz).to_json)
    assert_equal [ "First by pos", "Second by pos" ], parsed["questions"][0]["options"].map { |o| o["text"] }
  end
end

**Deep Dive into the Timer Specification**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. First, the core functionality: a timer for quiz questions, driven by "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" settings. Zero for both means no timer, a simple and clear default. The moderator's screen displays a countdown in M:SS format; the players *don't* see it. The countdown begins when a question opens and doesn't restart on page reload – that's crucial for avoiding unexpected behavior. At zero, the question automatically finishes. This automatic finish is a key UX point; it should mimic the moderator's "Finish" action. No surprises or deadlocks. Finally, this timer setting is *specific* to Quizzy itself, not part of any export – a nice isolation of the feature.

Now, let's overlay the general requirements. I need to be exact with labels: the auto-tests are unforgiving on those. The fact that the auto-tests depend on specific labels in quotes is something I can't let slide. I have to keep them consistent! And I have to keep the specific UI elements that the tests check, like lists inside of list items and the other specific requirements.

Let's dive into the implementation! The "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" settings need a home in the UI. Looking at the existing structure, the `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` partial is the key, shared between both "New quiz" and the "Settings" views. This is where I'll introduce them. Like `winners_count`, the timer settings should be present in both contexts. This way, they default to 0 and 0, and the moderator can either define them during quiz creation or adjust them later in settings. This makes logical sense. It's the cleanest approach.

Before I touch any code, let's perform some due diligence. I need to review existing tests to make sure this change doesn't break anything. I'll meticulously check `test/system/moderator_workflow_test.rb`, `test/system/edge_cases_test.rb`, and `test/system/prizes_and_leaderboard_test.rb` to ensure that this addition won't cause any regressions. **Analyzing Timer Settings: Database, Validation, and Input Handling**

Okay, so I'm looking at how consistently `prizes_and_leaderboard_test.rb` is structured. This is good; it helps me understand the project's style. I need to think carefully about how to add timer settings to the quiz. I see that when "Number of winners" was added, it was included in the `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` file.

Now, I'm diving into the data model for the timer settings. The question is, how do I store these settings on both `quizzes` and `games`? I'm considering storing `timer_minutes` and `timer_seconds` on the `quizzes` and then, possibly, snapshotting the total time in seconds on the `games` – or maybe storing both. But, what happens if someone enters `0` for minutes and `90` for seconds? Or `1` minute and `30` seconds? I have to analyze these edge cases very carefully to design this right.

What validations will be needed for "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds"? I re-read the prompt and see the requirement is for numbers. Specifically, *numbers* with the default being 0. That's a good starting point. I need to make sure I consider negative inputs, too.

Let's break down the input cases:

1.  **Default:** Both are `0`. These will be presented as `<input type="number">` fields.
2.  **Validations:**
    *   `timer_minutes` should be an integer, greater than or equal to 0. Negative values are invalid.
    *   `timer_seconds` should also be an integer, greater than or equal to 0. Negative values are invalid.

Here's where it gets interesting: what about `timer_seconds >= 60`? This is a great place to think like a tester and *thoroughly* analyze the possibilities.

Should `timer_seconds` allow 0-59 (like a typical form input), or should it accept values >= 60? Why are there *two* fields? Because minutes and seconds are standard time components. If I were designing this, I'd expect an entry of 1:30 (1 minute and 30 seconds) to be entered correctly, as 1 and 30. How would a QA tester test cases? How does the test code think about invalid inputs? I need to think carefully about what's expected for invalid input values. If there is a need to test invalid input, does it validate and reject `timer_seconds = 60` or is that accepted, and the value is corrected?

**Analyzing Timer Implementation for Quizzy**

Okay, let's break this down. We need to implement a timer for quiz questions, and the design choices here are key. The core of this is the storage and validation of the timer duration. We have two main approaches in mind: storing minutes and seconds separately on the `quizzes` table, or storing the total duration in seconds. The former needs careful validation, especially around the second's upper bound (e.g. `<= 59` vs allowing values like `90`), while the second approach will handle the total duration, with virtual accessors, `timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`.

Considering validation, it's clear we have to think about what is *actually* in the spec and how a QA test might be written. A critical point is this: the prompt says the fields are numbers with a default of 0. It does not explicitly mention that `timer_seconds` must be less than or equal to 59. Nor does it state any specific format for user-facing input. We've got to carefully consider the edge cases, especially around user experience: what happens when someone enters `0` minutes, `90` seconds, etc.? For example, if someone enters `0` minutes and `90` seconds, should we accept this and render "1:30" or require them to re-enter it?

The spec emphasizes the M:SS format on the moderator's screen, and that "0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer". So, we shouldn't limit the input for timer seconds to 59, because allowing 60 or more simplifies handling of total duration while accurately representing what is *required* in the prompt. We must be rigorous with validation: non-integers, negative numbers, and null values should be rejected. We can't let invalid data sneak into the database. Specifically: `presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }`.

I must consider the `Number of winners` field, which has `presence: true` and rejects blank input to inform our design. So, the blankness is best handled by `presence: true` validation on `timer_minutes` and `timer_seconds` too. And, based on how the application already deals with a "0" default for the `Number of winners`, blank input for the timers should not be treated as 0.

Based on the prompt, it would be a spec violation to reject the `timer_seconds` as 60 or greater, when the spec does not say this. Instead, we must let a moderator specify a total duration by allowing a value >= 0 for both minutes and seconds, and validate that with integer and positive checks. The total seconds should be snapshotted in `Game` when the game is started for consistency.

Now, thinking about `Game`, we need to snapshot the `question_timer_seconds` (total seconds) from the `quiz` to `game` at `Game.start_for_quiz!`. This ensures that quiz setting changes during a live game don't impact the live game. This parallels `winners_count`. When a question opens, we must set `opened_at` (datetime) on the `game_questions` table.

The main question is how to determine the countdown end. Should we store `timer_ends_at` (optional column, nullable) in the `game_questions` table, or compute it as `opened_at + game.question_timer_seconds`?
- Compute end time: Has the advantage of a single source of truth (`opened_at` and `game.question_timer_seconds`).
- There is no need for a nullable column!
- Computing eliminates data drift.

**Timer Architecture: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so the `opened_at` timestamp in SQLite uses microsecond precision, which is critical. I need to get this timer system absolutely right, particularly when the timer hits zero. It's a complex dance across the moderator's display, server-side enforcement, the player's view, and the ever-present problem of clock skew and Wi-Fi latency. Let's break it down methodically.

First, clock skew. The server *must* send the remaining time *relative to itself*, not a fixed end time. Forget sending just `ends_at` and let the browser calculate. The server will instead broadcast `remaining_ms` (milliseconds remaining) and `server_now` so the client can anchor to it using `performance.now()`. This `remaining_ms` is the key. It's a monotonic deadline: `localDeadlineMs = performance.now() + state.timer.remaining_ms`. Initial render uses server-side data, ensuring the display is correct from the start. Any server updates tighten this deadline, ensuring accuracy even when there is latency in updates. And using `Math.min` ensures we never push the timer *forward*, only *back*. Any latency, a sleeping laptop, and browser reloads is handled. That's a huge win!

Second, the display formula. `Math.ceil` is the *only* correct choice. This ensures the timer displays the full second. A timer set to `"0:05"` should display `"0:05"` for as long as possible. The visual tick needs to be frequent (every 100ms) but only re-render the DOM if the seconds have changed.

Third, server-side auto-finish is non-negotiable. If the moderator closes the browser, the server *must* still finish the question. The server also MUST handle late answer submissions. Let's design `GameTimer` to do the heavy lifting. I need a single lightweight scheduler thread using a `Mutex` and a `ConditionVariable` for the entire server. This is efficient and race-free. `GameTimer.schedule`, `GameTimer.cancel`, and the scheduler loop need to be meticulously designed to be race-free and exact, with no chance for a stale timer closing a question. Critically, within the database transaction, I must ensure atomic updates using an `UPDATE` with a `WHERE` clause. This way, if a moderator clicks "Finish" at the exact same time as the timer, the database will handle the race, ensuring that only one update succeeds, and we don't end up with a double-broadcast. And don't forget the need to check `question_timer_expired?` too. I want to be *sure* a timer can't close a question early because of a clock drift!

Finally, test everything. I *must* account for server restarts. I must ensure the server either recovers games or reschedules them to be sure the timers will fire when they should. A `GameTimer.recover_open_games!` and `@game.expire_timer_if_needed!` will do the trick. The moderator's browser must also have fallback to sync the state if the connection drops. The edge cases, from server restarts, clock skew, moderator screen reloads, the moderator clicking "Finish" early, and system and unit tests must *all* be rock-solid and bulletproof! `GameTimer.reset!` must be called to ensure tests remain atomic across threads. This architecture will deliver a seamless experience, no matter the circumstances.

It looks like Rails locks the thread connection, essentially sharing the *same* SQLite connection across all threads within the test process. This contrasts sharply with `ActiveSupport::TestCase` (unit/integration tests) where no thread locking occurs, and `ActionDispatch::SystemTestCase`, which pins the connection. It makes sense, given the intention of system tests.

Now, zooming in on `GameTimer`: wrapping `GameTimer.finish_expired_game` with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection` and a `rescue StandardError` is excellent defensive programming. It elegantly handles potential `RecordNotFound` or `nil` scenarios that can arise from transactional rollbacks in unit tests before the `teardown` process can fully complete with `GameTimer.reset!`. Also, scheduling `GameTimer.schedule(...)` *after* the database transaction commits in `Game#start!` and `Game#next_question!` is brilliant. This prevents scheduling phantom timers if the transaction rolls back, and ensures that the data the timer relies on is actually committed before the background thread accesses it. And even better, calling `GameTimer.cancel(id)` after the transaction returns `true` cleanly cancels the timer.

The next point I examined was the choice of sleep duration measurement. Employing `Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` to measure the sleep duration relative to a time deadline, while still verifying against `Time.current` in `Game#expire_timer_if_needed!` is clever. I realized that a slight granularity discrepancy between the monotonic clock and `Time.current` could lead to errors. I traced that bug through the code. So, the `Time.current` check *after* the monotonic clock is critical. This approach elegantly handles all the edge cases where the wall clock might jump backward.

Finally, what about unit tests using `travel_to`? Because the `GameTimer` background thread sleeps in real-time, the test will advance the `Time.current`, causing `expire_timer_if_needed!` to finish the question, cancel the timer, and broadcast immediately, and `GameTimer.reset!` clears `@scheduled` in teardown. However, transactional unit tests that take longer than the timer's duration may hit SQLite lock if the test thread still has an open transaction. class GameTimer
  class << self
    def schedule(game_id:, question_id:, ends_at:)
      return unless ends_at

      mutex.synchronize do
        scheduled[game_id] = { question_id: question_id, ends_at: ends_at }
        condition.signal
      end
      ensure_thread_started
    end

    def ensure_scheduled(game, question: nil)
      return unless game&.timer_enabled? && game.question_open?

      q = question || game.current_question
      return unless q

      ends_at = game.question_timer_ends_at(q)
      return unless ends_at

      needs_start = false
      mutex.synchronize do
        existing = scheduled[game.id]
        unless existing && existing[:question_id] == q.id && existing[:ends_at] == ends_at
          scheduled[game.id] = { question_id: q.id, ends_at: ends_at }
          condition.signal
        end
        needs_start = !@thread&.alive?
      end
      ensure_thread_started if needs_start
    end

    def cancel(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        removed = scheduled.delete(game_id)
        condition.signal if removed
      end
    end

    def scheduled_entry(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize { scheduled[game_id]&.dup }
    end

    def recover_open_games!
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        return unless ActiveRecord::Base.connection.data_source_exists?("games")

        Game.includes(:quiz, game_questions: :game_options)
            .where(status: "question_open")
            .where("question_timer_seconds > 0")
            .find_each do |game|
              game.expire_timer_if_needed!
            end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GameTimer] recovery error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        scheduled.clear
        condition.signal
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def condition
      @condition ||= ConditionVariable.new
    end

    def scheduled
      @scheduled ||= {}
    end

    def thread_mutex
      @thread_mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def ensure_thread_started
      return if @thread&.alive?

      thread_mutex.synchronize do
        return if @thread&.alive?

        @thread = Thread.new do
          Thread.current.name = "game-timer"
          run_loop
        end
      end
    end

    def run_loop
      loop do
        due_items = wait_for_due_items
        due_items.each do |game_id, question_id|
          process_due_item(game_id, question_id)
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GameTimer] loop error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      sleep 0.2
      retry
    end

    def wait_for_due_items
      mutex.synchronize do
        loop do
          if scheduled.empty?
            condition.wait(mutex)
            next
          end

          now = Time.current
          due = []
          next_deadline = nil

          scheduled.each do |game_id, meta|
            if meta[:ends_at] <= now
              due << [ game_id, meta[:question_id] ]
            elsif next_deadline.nil? || meta[:ends_at] < next_deadline
              next_deadline = meta[:ends_at]
            end
          end

          if due.any?
            due.each { |game_id, _| scheduled.delete(game_id) }
            return due
          end

          wait_seconds = [ next_deadline - now, 0.005 ].max
          condition.wait(mutex, wait_seconds)
        end
      end
    end

    def process_due_item(game_id, question_id)
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        game = Game.includes(:quiz, game_questions: :game_options).find_by(id: game_id)
        return unless game

        game.expire_timer_if_needed!(expected_question_id: question_id)
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GameTimer] finish error for game #{game_id}: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "securerandom"
require "set"

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :winners_count,
    presence: true,
    numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, allow_blank: true }
  validates :question_timer_seconds,
    presence: true,
    numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0, allow_blank: true }

  after_destroy_commit { GameTimer.cancel(id) }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Quiz has no active questions" if active.empty?

    attempts = 0
    begin
      attempts += 1
      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(
          code: generate_code,
          status: "lobby",
          winners_count: quiz.winners_count,
          question_timer_seconds: quiz.question_timer_seconds
        )

        active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question: question,
            position: q_index + 1,
            body: question.body
          )

          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              option: option,
              position: o_index + 1,
              body: option.body,
              correct: option.correct?
            )
          end
        end

        game
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      raise if attempts >= 5
      retry
    end
  end

  def self.generate_code
    Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
  end

  def self.player_cookie_name(code)
    "quizzy_player_#{code.to_s.upcase}"
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def timer_enabled?
    question_timer_seconds.to_i > 0
  end

  def question_timer_ends_at(question = current_question)
    return nil unless timer_enabled? && question

    opened = question.opened_at || started_at || question.created_at
    return nil unless opened

    opened + question_timer_seconds.seconds
  end

  def question_timer_remaining_ms(question = current_question, now: Time.current)
    ends_at = question_timer_ends_at(question)
    return nil unless ends_at

    [ ((ends_at - now) * 1000).round, 0 ].max
  end

  def question_timer_expired?(question = current_question, now: Time.current)
    ends_at = question_timer_ends_at(question)
    return false unless ends_at

    now >= ends_at
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_index.present? && current_question_index >= total_questions - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_question_answers_count
    q = current_question
    return 0 unless q

    answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count
  end

  def start!
    opened_question = nil
    started = transaction do
      reload
      return false unless lobby?

      questions = ordered_questions
      return false if questions.empty?

      now = Time.current
      opened_question = questions.first
      opened_question.update!(opened_at: now)
      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: 0, started_at: now)
      true
    end

    if started && timer_enabled? && opened_question
      GameTimer.schedule(
        game_id: id,
        question_id: opened_question.id,
        ends_at: question_timer_ends_at(opened_question)
      )
    end

    started
  end

  def finish_question!(expected_question_id: nil)
    transitioned = transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_open?

      q = current_question
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && q&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      rows = Game.where(
        id: id,
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: current_question_index
      ).update_all(status: "question_closed", updated_at: Time.current)

      reload
      rows == 1
    end

    GameTimer.cancel(id) if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def expire_timer_if_needed!(expected_question_id: nil, broadcast: true)
    return false unless timer_enabled? && question_open?

    q = current_question
    return false unless q
    return false if expected_question_id.present? && q.id != expected_question_id.to_i

    unless question_timer_expired?(q)
      GameTimer.ensure_scheduled(self, question: q)
      return false
    end

    transitioned = finish_question!(expected_question_id: q.id)
    broadcast_all! if transitioned && broadcast
    transitioned
  end

  def next_question!(expected_question_id: nil)
    opened_question = nil
    transitioned = transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed?

      questions = ordered_questions
      return false if current_question_index.nil? || current_question_index >= questions.size - 1
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && questions[current_question_index]&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      next_index = current_question_index + 1
      opened_question = questions[next_index]
      opened_question.update!(opened_at: Time.current)
      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: next_index)
      true
    end

    if transitioned && timer_enabled? && opened_question
      GameTimer.schedule(
        game_id: id,
        question_id: opened_question.id,
        ends_at: question_timer_ends_at(opened_question)
      )
    end

    transitioned
  end

  def end_game!(expected_question_id: nil)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed? && last_question?
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && current_question&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      update!(status: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
      true
    end
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    transaction do
      reload
      return nil unless question_open?

      q = current_question
      return nil unless q && q.id == game_question_id.to_i

      now = Time.current
      return nil if question_timer_expired?(q, now: now)

      opt = q.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      return nil unless opt

      Answer.upsert(
        {
          game_id: id,
          player_id: player.id,
          game_question_id: q.id,
          game_option_id: opt.id,
          answered_at: now,
          created_at: now,
          updated_at: now
        },
        unique_by: %i[player_id game_question_id]
      )
      opt.id
    end
  end

  def leaderboard
    game_players = players.order(:id).to_a
    return [] if game_players.empty?

    opened_at_by_question_id = game_questions.pluck(:id, :opened_at, :created_at).each_with_object({}) do |(gq_id, opened_at, created_at), map|
      map[gq_id] = opened_at || started_at || created_at
    end

    stats_by_player_id = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { points: 0, correct_time_us: 0 } }

    answers
      .joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_options: { correct: true })
      .pluck(:player_id, :game_question_id, :answered_at, :updated_at)
      .each do |player_id, gq_id, answered_at, updated_at|
        stat = stats_by_player_id[player_id]
        stat[:points] += 1
        q_opened = opened_at_by_question_id[gq_id]
        pick_time = answered_at || updated_at
        if q_opened && pick_time
          elapsed_us = ((pick_time - q_opened) * 1_000_000).round
          stat[:correct_time_us] += elapsed_us if elapsed_us > 0
        end
      end

    ranked = game_players.map do |player|
      stat = stats_by_player_id[player.id]
      {
        player_id: player.id,
        name: player.name,
        points: stat[:points],
        correct_time_us: stat[:correct_time_us],
        winner: player.winner?
      }
    end

    ranked.sort_by! { |entry| [ -entry[:points], entry[:correct_time_us], entry[:player_id] ] }

    ranked.each_with_index do |entry, index|
      entry[:place] = index + 1
    end

    ranked
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      board = leaderboard
      winner_ids = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }.first(winners_count).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: SecureRandom)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      board = leaderboard
      eligible = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }

      winner_ids = if eligible.size <= winners_count
                     eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      else
                     cutoff_points = board[winners_count - 1][:points]
                     guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
                     remaining = winners_count - guaranteed.size
                     tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
                     drawn = tied_pool.sample(remaining, random: random)
                     (guaranteed + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      end

      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def reset_winners!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      apply_winners!([])
      true
    end
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:moderator"
  end

  def players_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:players"
  end

  def visitors_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:visitors"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player_id)
    "game:#{id}:player:#{player_id}"
  end

  def moderator_state(board: nil)
    total = total_questions
    active_count = active_players_count

    base = {
      game_id: id,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      active_players_count: active_count,
      total_questions: total,
      winners_count: winners_count,
      winners_version: winners_version
    }

    case status
    when "lobby"
      base.merge(players_count: active_count)
    when "question_open"
      q = current_question
      answers_count = q ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count : 0
      state = base.merge(
        answers_count: answers_count,
        question: serialize_open_question(q, current_question_index, total)
      )
      if timer_enabled? && q
        now = Time.current
        ends_at = question_timer_ends_at(q)
        state[:timer] = {
          duration_seconds: question_timer_seconds,
          remaining_ms: question_timer_remaining_ms(q, now: now),
          ends_at: ends_at.iso8601(3)
        }
      end
      state
    when "question_closed"
      q = current_question
      counts_by_option = q ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).group(:game_option_id).count : {}
      total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
      base.merge(
        answers_count: total_answers,
        question: serialize_closed_moderator_question(q, current_question_index, total, counts_by_option, total_answers)
      )
    when "finished"
      board ||= leaderboard
      tied_ids = tied_cutoff_player_ids(board)
      base.merge(
        leaderboard: board.map do |entry|
          {
            player_id: entry[:player_id],
            place: entry[:place],
            name: entry[:name],
            points: entry[:points],
            winner: entry[:winner],
            tied_at_cutoff: tied_ids.include?(entry[:player_id])
          }
        end
      )
    else
      base
    end
  end

  def public_player_state
    total = total_questions
    base = {
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status
    }

    case status
    when "question_open"
      q = current_question
      base.merge(question: serialize_open_question(q, current_question_index, total))
    when "question_closed"
      q = current_question
      base.merge(question: serialize_closed_player_question(q, current_question_index, total))
    when "finished"
      base.merge(winners_version: winners_version)
    else
      base
    end
  end

  def player_state(player, board: nil)
    state = public_player_state.merge(
      joined: true,
      player: {
        id: player.id,
        name: player.name
      }
    )

    if question_open?
      q = current_question
      return state unless q

      answer = answers.find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      state.merge(selected_option_id: answer&.game_option_id)
    elsif question_closed?
      q = current_question
      return state unless q

      answer = answers.includes(:game_option).find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      outcome = if answer.nil?
                  "no_answer"
      elsif answer.game_option.correct?
                  "correct"
      else
                  "wrong"
      end
      state.merge(
        selected_option_id: answer&.game_option_id,
        outcome: outcome
      )
    elsif finished?
      board ||= leaderboard
      entry = board.find { |e| e[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        state.merge(
          place: entry[:place],
          total_players: board.size,
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        )
      else
        state
      end
    else
      state
    end
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_state!(board: nil)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state(board: board))
  end

  def broadcast_all!
    if finished?
      broadcast_finished_state!
    else
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(players_stream_name, public_player_state)
      broadcast_moderator_state!
    end
  end

  def broadcast_finished_state!
    board = leaderboard
    broadcast_moderator_state!(board: board)

    pub_finished = {
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      winners_version: winners_version
    }

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(visitors_stream_name, pub_finished)

    total_players = board.size
    board.each do |entry|
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        player_stream_name(entry[:player_id]),
        pub_finished.merge(
          joined: true,
          player: {
            id: entry[:player_id],
            name: entry[:name]
          },
          place: entry[:place],
          total_players: total_players,
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        )
      )
    end
  end

  def broadcast_player_answer!(player_id, game_question_id, selected_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      player_stream_name(player_id),
      {
        type: "answer_updated",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: selected_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def apply_winners!(winner_ids)
    players.where(winner: true).update_all(winner: false)
    players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
    players.reset
    update!(winners_version: winners_version + 1)
  end

  def tied_cutoff_player_ids(board)
    eligible = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }
    return Set.new if eligible.size <= winners_count

    cutoff_points = board[winners_count - 1][:points]
    guaranteed_count = eligible.count { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
    remaining = winners_count - guaranteed_count
    tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }

    return Set.new if tied_pool.size <= remaining

    tied_pool.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }.to_set
  end

  def serialize_open_question(q, idx, total)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def serialize_closed_player_question(q, idx, total)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body,
          correct: opt.correct?
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def serialize_closed_moderator_question(q, idx, total, counts_by_option, total_answers)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      is_last: idx >= total - 1,
      total_answers: total_answers,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        count = counts_by_option[opt.id] || 0
        share = total_answers > 0 ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round : 0
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body,
          correct: opt.correct?,
          count: count,
          share: share
        }
      end
    }
  end
end

    before_action :set_game

        @player_stream_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, @player.id ])

        @join_form_player = @game.players.new
      end

        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      if @player
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      @join_form_player = @game.players.new(name: join_name_param)

      if @join_form_player.save
        cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)] = {
          value: @join_form_player.token,
          httponly: true,
          same_site: :lax,
          expires: 7.days.from_now
        }
        touch_player_presence(@join_form_player)
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def state
      @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        render json: @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        render json: @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
      end
    end

    def answer
      unless @player
        render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
        return
      end

      game_question_id = params[:game_question_id].to_i
      game_option_id = params[:game_option_id].to_i

      selected_id = @game.submit_answer!(
        player: @player,
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        game_option_id: game_option_id
      )

      if selected_id
        GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state!
        @game.broadcast_player_answer!(@player.id, game_question_id, selected_id)
        render json: {
          ok: true,
          game_question_id: game_question_id,
          selected_option_id: selected_id
        }
      else
        @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
        @game.reload
        render json: {
          ok: false,
          state: @game.player_state(@player)
        }, status: :conflict
      end
    end

    def leave
      if @player
        changed, _count = GamePresence.leave_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end

      head :no_content
    end

    private

    def set_no_store_cache
      response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    end

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    end

    def load_player
      token = cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)]
      @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
    end

    def touch_player_presence(player)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, player.id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)

      return player_param[:name].to_s if player_param.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || player_param.is_a?(Hash)

      params[:name].to_s
    end
  end

class ModeratorChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(id: params[:game_id])
    unless @game && authorized_moderator?(@game.id)
      reject
      return
    end

    @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
    stream_from @game.moderator_stream_name
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def authorized_moderator?(game_id)
    return true if connection.moderator_authenticated

    token = params[:token].to_s
    return false if token.empty?

    verified_game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).verified(token)
    verified_game_id.present? && verified_game_id.to_i == game_id
  end
end

class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    @subscription_key = "#{connection.connection_id}:#{object_id}"
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      unless @game.finished?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      stream_from @game.visitors_stream_name
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    @game.reload
    return if @game.finished?

    @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    @game.expire_timer_if_needed!
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end
EOF

class LiveGameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase

  test "ModeratorChannel rejects unauthorized subscribers and accepts valid signed token" do
    self.class.tests ModeratorChannel

    stub_connection(connection_id: "c1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    wrong_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id + 999)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: wrong_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    valid_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: valid_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end

  test "PlayerChannel tracks presence for joined player and ignores anonymous visitor" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    # Anonymous visitor does not increment active players and gets visitors stream
    stub_connection(connection_id: "anon-1", moderator_authenticated: false)

    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?

    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
    unsubscribe

    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, player.id ])

    stub_connection(connection_id: "alice-1", moderator_authenticated: false)

    subscribe(code: @game.code, player_token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.player_stream_name(player.id)
    assert_equal 1, @game.active_players_count
    assert_equal "Alice", transmissions.last.dig(:player, :name)

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
  end

  test "PlayerChannel streams finished results and winner updates for joined players" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    @game.start!
    q = @game.current_question
    @game.submit_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: q.game_options.find_by!(correct: true).id)

messages.thinking:
**My Testing Crusade**

Okay, time to really lock down the timer functionality with some serious testing. I'm thinking comprehensive coverage here – unit, model, integration, channel, *and* system tests, the whole shebang. Let's start with a solid foundation and build up.

First, I need to flesh out `quiz_test.rb`. Making sure those timer-related defaults are correct and that validations and helpers are rock solid. Then, I'll carve out a specific test for the quiz exporter, `quiz/exporter_test.rb`, ensuring the timer is correctly *excluded* from the export format, which is critical.

Next, a brand new `game_timer_test.rb` is essential. This will be the heart of it, focusing on the mechanics: scheduling, cancellation, real-time firing, handling stale questions, proper recovery, capturing game timer snapshots, expiration, late answer rejection – the works. I need to nail down the isolation of moderator versus player payloads in all scenarios.

Then, I'll dive into an `integration/timer_test.rb` to cover the user experience. This means the settings form and validation need testing. We need SSR (server-side rendering) timer display and making sure it persists through reloads. We'll be testing auto-finish behavior on state fetches and what happens when answers come in late. I *must* ensure zero timer leakage to players through HTML/JSON responses and that export/import functions maintain isolation.

The channels are critical, so I'll also update `live_game_channels_test.rb`. Specifically, I'll focus on the moderator channel with the timer payload and expiration and for the player channel with zero timer leakage and expiration.

Finally, the grand finale: a comprehensive `system/timer_test.rb` suite using Chromium. We'll simulate the user experience from end-to-end, testing the settings, accessibility, export exclusion, and the "no-timer" behavior in the absence of a timer. We need to verify proper 1:30 formatting and early finish scenarios. And make sure that players *never* see the timer (unless we want them to!). The timer should not restart on reload. The auto-finish needs to work across moderator, projector, and player tabs when it reaches 0:00, including the corner case of a server-side auto-finish when the moderator tab is even closed.

I think writing the model, integration, and channel tests is the right way to start building up.

require "test_helper"

class GameTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Timer Model Quiz", timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Question 1", active: true)
    q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Right 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Wrong 1", correct: false }
    ])
    q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Question 2", active: true)
    q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Wrong 2", correct: false },
      { body: "Right 2", correct: true }
    ])
  end

  test "snapshots question_timer_seconds at game start and isolates moderator vs player payloads" do
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_equal 90, game.question_timer_seconds
    assert game.timer_enabled?

    # Changing quiz settings later does not affect the already-started game
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    assert_equal 90, game.reload.question_timer_seconds

    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")

    # Lobby: no timer on moderator or player
    assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer]
    assert_not game.public_player_state.key?(:timer)
    assert_not game.player_state(player).key?(:timer)

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 14:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0, with_usec: true) do
      assert game.start!
      mod = game.moderator_state
      assert_equal 90, mod.dig(:timer, :duration_seconds)
      assert_equal 90_000, mod.dig(:timer, :remaining_ms)
      assert_equal (t0 + 90.seconds).iso8601(3), mod.dig(:timer, :ends_at)

      # Players NEVER receive timer fields
      assert_not game.public_player_state.key?(:timer)
      assert_not game.player_state(player).key?(:timer)
      assert_not game.player_state(player)[:question].key?(:opened_at)
    end

    # Advancing time reduces remaining_ms without resetting opened_at
    travel_to(t0 + 25.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert_equal 65_000, game.moderator_state.dig(:timer, :remaining_ms)
      assert_not game.expire_timer_if_needed!
      assert game.question_open?
    end

    # After deadline, expire_timer_if_needed! closes the question once and removes timer from state
    travel_to(t0 + 90.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert game.expire_timer_if_needed!(broadcast: false)
      assert game.question_closed?
      assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer]
      assert_not game.expire_timer_if_needed!(broadcast: false)
    end
  end

  test "zero timer disables countdown and never auto-finishes" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_equal 0, game.question_timer_seconds
    assert_not game.timer_enabled?

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 14:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0, with_usec: true) { assert game.start! }
    assert_nil GameTimer.scheduled_entry(game.id)
    assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer]

    travel_to(t0 + 1.hour, with_usec: true) do
      assert_not game.expire_timer_if_needed!(broadcast: false)
      assert game.question_open?
    end
  end

  test "submit_answer! rejects answers at or after deadline and preserves prior pick" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 10)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 14:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0, with_usec: true) { game.start! }
    q = game.current_question
    right = q.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
    wrong = q.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)

    # Valid pick at t + 4s
    travel_to(t0 + 4.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert_equal right.id, game.submit_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: right.id)
    end

    # Late re-pick at t + 10s (exact deadline) rejected; original answer preserved
    travel_to(t0 + 10.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert_nil game.submit_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: wrong.id)
      assert_equal right.id, game.answers.find_by!(player: player, game_question: q).game_option_id
    end
  end

  test "early finish cancels scheduled timer and next question schedules a fresh timer" do
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 14:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0, with_usec: true) do
      assert game.start!
      q1 = game.current_question
      entry = GameTimer.scheduled_entry(game.id)
      assert_equal q1.id, entry[:question_id]
      assert_in_delta (t0 + 90.seconds).to_f, entry[:ends_at].to_f, 0.001
    end

    # Moderator clicks Finish early at t0 + 15s
    travel_to(t0 + 15.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert game.finish_question!
      assert_nil GameTimer.scheduled_entry(game.id)
      assert game.question_closed?
    end

    # Moderator opens Question 2 at t0 + 30s -> fresh 90s timer ending at t0 + 120s
    travel_to(t0 + 30.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert game.next_question!
      q2 = game.current_question
      entry = GameTimer.scheduled_entry(game.id)
      assert_equal q2.id, entry[:question_id]
      assert_in_delta (t0 + 120.seconds).to_f, entry[:ends_at].to_f, 0.001
      assert_equal 90_000, game.moderator_state.dig(:timer, :remaining_ms)
    end

    # Deleting game cancels scheduled timer
    game_id = game.id
    game.destroy!
    assert_nil GameTimer.scheduled_entry(game_id)
  end

  test "stale expected_question_id cannot expire a newer question" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 5)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 14:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0, with_usec: true) { game.start! }
    q1 = game.current_question
    travel_to(t0 + 1.second, with_usec: true) { game.finish_question! }
    travel_to(t0 + 2.seconds, with_usec: true) { game.next_question! }
    q2 = game.current_question

    # At t0 + 6s (q1 would have expired, q2 still has 1s left)
    travel_to(t0 + 6.seconds, with_usec: true) do
      assert_not game.expire_timer_if_needed!(expected_question_id: q1.id, broadcast: false)
      assert game.question_open?
      assert_equal q2.id, game.current_question.id
    end
  end
end

class GameTimerBackgroundExecutionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  self.use_transactional_tests = false

  teardown do
    GameTimer.reset!
    Quiz.where(title: "Real Time Timer Quiz").destroy_all
  end

  test "GameTimer automatically closes an open question in real time and recover_open_games! catches expired games" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Real Time Timer Quiz", timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 1)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Fast question?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Yes", correct: true },
      { body: "No", correct: false }
    ])

    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    assert game.start!
    assert game.question_open?

    # Wait up to 2.5s for background GameTimer thread to auto-close the game
    deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 2.5
    loop do
      break if game.reload.question_closed?
      break if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
      sleep 0.05
    end
    assert game.reload.question_closed?, "Expected GameTimer background thread to auto-finish the question"

    # Also test recover_open_games! on a game that already expired while unscheduled
    game2 = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game2.start!
    GameTimer.reset!
    game2.current_question.update!(opened_at: 5.seconds.ago)
    assert game2.reload.question_open?

    GameTimer.recover_open_games!
    assert game2.reload.question_closed?
  end
end
